routes.name: Royal Nin & Queen's Beach family loop
routes.surface: Paved local roads and the coastal cycle path between Sabunike/Privlaka and Nin; old-town streets of Nin are paved stone and get crowded in July-August, so walk the bike through the centre at peak times.
highlights: Sabunike viewpoint over the shallow sandy bay (marked on the official T&F Privlaka 1 route)
Kraljičina plaža (Queen's Beach): long sandy beach with very shallow water, ideal stop with small children
Nin old town on its island, reached over small bridges; Church of the Holy Cross, often called the smallest cathedral in the world
Nin salt works (Solana Nin) at the edge of the lagoon
routes.windNote: Dead flat and fully exposed. A NE bura or the summer afternoon NW breeze blows across the lagoon road; with small kids ride it in the morning or at sunset when the wind usually drops.
routes.description: A 45-minute, almost perfectly flat loop that every family can ride: out of the driveway, past the Sabunike viewpoint, to Queen's Beach for a swim and into the 3,000-year-old royal town of Nin for ice cream. It closely follows the official T&F Nin 1 family route (Nin-Privlaka-Sabunike, 12.6 km, 32 m).

routes.name: Privlaka peninsula & Vir island ride
routes.surface: Asphalt throughout (local roads and the main Privlaka-Vir road). The Vir bridge has only a narrow strip next to the railing that is not separated from traffic; families should walk across on it, road riders should take the lane.
highlights: Privlaka old centre, presented by the tourist board as the westernmost point of Dalmatia
Vir bridge with views over the coastal marshes
Bandira (112 m), the highest point of Vir, with views to Pag and the Zadar archipelago
Sand and pebble beaches in pine woods along the Vir shore

waypoints.name: West Vir road end (near Lanterna lighthouse)

routes.windNote: The Vir bridge is notoriously windy (rider tip: "watch out for the wind"). Avoid crossing with kids on days with strong bura (NE) gusts.
routes.description: A relaxed half-day out to the island next door: through Privlaka, over the Vir bridge and across Vir to the quiet west end near the Lanterna lighthouse, with a climb to Bandira, the island high point, for the view. It combines the official T&F Privlaka 1 and T&F Vir routes; the official 16.4 km round-Vir loop (188 m) can be added for a longer day.

routes.name: Vrsi coves gravel: Ričina, Duboka Draga & Ljubač fortress
routes.surface: Mixed: asphalt village roads plus macadam (gravel) farm and coastal tracks around Vrsi, Ljubač and Poljica. Router-generated line: surface of individual segments not verified, ride it on 35 mm+ tyres or an MTB.
highlights: Vrsi village above the Nin lagoon with views of Velebit and the towers of Nin
Uvala Ričina: pine-shaded local beaches (official T&F Nin 2 route)
Rt Jasenovo and the Jasenovo viewpoint (official MTB Grand route)
Duboka Draga cove: deep, clear water and a favourite snorkelling stop
Gradina Ljubljana: ruins of the Ljubač hill fort above the Ljubač bay
Ljubač bay and the fields of Poljica on the way home
routes.windNote: Partly sheltered by pine woods and low hills; the Ljubač headland is exposed to bura blowing down from Velebit across the channel.
routes.description: A swim-and-ride gravel day linking the hidden coves north-east of Nin: Ričina, the Jasenovo viewpoint and Duboka Draga (bring a mask), then up to the ruined hill fort above Ljubač bay and back through open fields. It overlaps the official MTB Grand route (Zaton-Vrsi-Jasenovo-Nin, 42.5 km, 320 m) and the T&F Nin 2 Vrsi-Ričina family route.

routes.name: Zadar coast ride to the Sea Organ
routes.surface: Asphalt. Coastal local roads through Zaton and Petrčane, then the Zadar suburbs (Diklo, Borik) and the city waterfront; return inland via Poljica on quiet farm roads.
highlights: Zaton and Petrčane bays and pine-shaded coastal roads
Zadar peninsula: the Sea Organ and the Greeting to the Sun on the waterfront
Coffee stop in Zadar's Roman/Venetian old town
Quiet return through the fields of the Zadar hinterland past Poljica and Grbe
routes.windNote: Southbound along the coast you usually ride into the afternoon NW maestral in summer; under bura (NE) the inland return through Poljica is a crosswind.
routes.description: A culture ride with a sea view most of the way: down the coast through Zaton and Petrčane to listen to the Sea Organ in Zadar, then home on near-empty roads across the fields. It mirrors the official Road Zadar route (Zadar-Petrčane-Nin-Vrsi, 44.7 km, 181 m) in reverse, starting at the villa.

routes.name: Pag bridge & the moon island: ride to Pag town
routes.surface: Asphalt. Local roads via Vrsi and Ljubač, then the D106 main road over the Pag bridge to Pag town; return via Ražanac and Poljica.
highlights: Pag bridge (Paški most): 301 m long with a 201 m arch rising 35 m above the Ljubačka vrata strait, opened 17 November 1968
Fortica fortress ruins guarding the bridge on the Pag side
Pag's bare, moon-like karst landscape shaped by the bura and salt spray
Pag town and the salt pans; Pag lace (UNESCO-listed) and Pag cheese
Ražanac on the return, with views across to Velebit and Paklenica
routes.windNote: The most wind-sensitive route here. A 198 km/h gust was recorded on the Pag bridge (2019) and the D106 bridge is closed to traffic in strong bura; check the forecast and skip it on bura days. No shade on Pag: carry plenty of water.
routes.description: The signature 'life on Mars' day: across the high arch of the Pag bridge onto the bare white rock of Pag island and along to the medieval salt town of Pag for lunch, returning along the Ražanac coast under Velebit. Pag-town loops from the official map (T&F 18 Pag via the salt pans, 18 km) can be added for a longer day.

routes.name: Ravni kotari villages & Novigrad Sea loop
routes.surface: Asphalt, mostly quiet county and village roads across the Ravni kotari plateau; short stretches on regional roads around Posedarje and Ražanac.
highlights: Stone villages and farmland of the Ravni kotari hinterland (Poljica-Brig, Poličnik, Islam Grčki)
Descent to Novigrad on the enclosed Novigrad Sea
Posedarje waterfront on the Novigrad Sea
Coastal return via Ražanac and Ljubač with Velebit always in view
routes.windNote: Open plateau with little shelter; on bura days the return along the Ražanac coast is a block headwind/crosswind from the NE.
routes.description: A rolling century-lite through the farmland of Ravni kotari, away from the coastal crowds: inland villages, a descent to the hidden Novigrad Sea, then back along the Velebit channel coast. Good for groups and e-bike tours that want empty roads and authentic village cafes.

routes.name: Paklenica & the Velebit Channel
routes.surface: Asphalt. Coast road via Ražanac to Posedarje, then the old Maslenica bridge (D8) and the D8 coastal road under Velebit to Starigrad-Paklenica; out-and-back on the D8.
highlights: Old Maslenica bridge (D8) high above the Novsko ždrilo gorge
The D8 coast road along the foot of Velebit with views across to Pag
Entrance to Paklenica National Park (Velika Paklenica canyon, a famous climbing area)
Starigrad-Paklenica waterfront for lunch
routes.windNote: Bura country: the Maslenica area holds the record bura gust of 248 km/h (21 Dec 1998, measured on the Maslenica motorway bridge). On days with a bura forecast this route is unsafe; on calm days it is spectacular.
routes.description: A big coastal day to the foot of Velebit: over the Maslenica bridge and along the Velebit channel to the mouth of the Paklenica canyon, where you can lock the bikes and walk into the gorge. Paklenica Riviera publishes local add-on loops (e.g. Route 1 Starigrad-Modrič).

routes.name: Velebit epic: Obrovac to the Mali Alan pass
suitableFor: strong road riders on wide tyres
routes.surface: Asphalt to Obrovac. The south climb from Obrovac (historic road named Majstorska cesta in OSM) is roughly half good asphalt and half rough gravel; per Quäldich the asphalt ends at about km 11.5 of the climb and the surface worsens after the wind wall at Tulove grede. Gravel bike (35 mm+) or MTB recommended, especially for the descent.
highlights: Obrovac and the Zrmanja river canyon
Long, lonely climb up the bare south face of Velebit, past war ruins in the lower part
Tulove grede rock towers just below the pass
Mali Alan pass (about 1,045 m), a remote crossing of the Velebit range
routes.windNote: Exposed high karst: bura can make the upper section unrideable, and expect the summit to be about 6-7 °C colder than the coast (standard lapse rate, about 1,000 m higher). The road is not cleared in winter. Go only on settled, bura-free days.
routes.description: The bucket-list climb from the villa: across Ravni kotari to Obrovac on the Zrmanja, then about 21 km and roughly 1,000 m of climbing on the old road up the bare south face of Velebit to the Mali Alan pass at about 1,045 m. A car-assisted version starting in Obrovac (about 42 km return) suits most riders.

variants.name: Car-assisted from Obrovac
variants.note: Out-and-back Obrovac to Mali Alan, about 21 km each way per the bike router, about 1,030 m gain per the DEM profile (Quäldich: 23 km, 1,039 m from the Zrmanja bridge).

bikeShopsAndRentals.description: Nearest rental, about 4 km from the villa. Offers bikes for all ages, child seats, helmets and maps, and advertises free delivery to your apartment address.

bikeShopsAndRentals.description: Bike rental inside the resort, open to non-guests (who must pay an entry fee to the grounds).

bikeShopsAndRentals.description: Bike, e-bike and scooter shop with workshop; services most bike types, also bikes bought elsewhere (out of warranty). Links to a separate rental site rent-a-bike-zadar.com.

bikeShopsAndRentals.description: Branch of the Croatian bike retail chain; OSM tags it with bicycle repair.

bikeShopsAndRentals.description: Bike shop in Zadar tagged in OSM with bicycle repair.

bikeShopsAndRentals.name: Zadar old-town bike rental (Špire Brusine 8)
bikeShopsAndRentals.description: City bike rental sold on Expedia/Pelago: 8-hour rental with helmet, lock and city map, child bikes and child seats; suggests the bike route to Nin.

publicRepairStations.description: Public tool/pump stand on the Pag, Paklenica and Ravni kotari routes.

publicRepairStations.description: Public repair stand near the turnaround of the Paklenica route.

publicRepairStations.description: Public repair stand (24/7 in OSM) on the D8 side of the Maslenica bridge.

seasonAndWeather.summary: Best riding: April-June and mid-September to October, with highs of 18-27 °C. March and November are mild (14-15 °C) but windier and wetter; November is the wettest month (about 205 mm, 14 rain days). July-August highs are about 30 °C: ride before 10:00. Bura (NE) days are commonest November-March.

winds.name: Bura (bora)
winds.description: Cold, gusty N-NE katabatic wind falling off Velebit; strongest in the Velebit channel, Maslenica, Pag and Senj. Record gust 248 km/h on the Maslenica motorway (A1) bridge (21 Dec 1998). Most common in winter; can last 2-3 days. Bura days are clear and dry but make bridges and the D8/D106 dangerous.

winds.name: Pag bridge closures
winds.description: In strong bura the D106 Pag bridge has been closed to all vehicles, or to high-sided vehicles and motorcycles, and Pag has been cut off from the mainland.

winds.name: Vir bridge
winds.description: Rider reports flag strong crosswinds and frequent traffic on the Vir bridge.

trafficNotes.text: The Nin-Privlaka-Vir road and the Vir bridge carry heavy traffic in July-August; the bridge has only a narrow strip by the railing, not separated from traffic. Road riders: take the lane; families: walk across.
Nin old town: cycling is allowed but not recommended at peak times; walk through the centre in summer.
D106 (Pag bridge, Pag island) and D8 (Maslenica-Starigrad) are main roads with trucks and summer traffic; much quieter March-June and September-November.
The county roads through Vrsi, Ljubač, Poljica and Ravni kotari are the quietest riding near the villa.
Velebit (Mali Alan): landmines remain in parts of the range; never leave the road or gravel track. The Mali Alan road is not cleared in winter.

roadRules.rule: Cyclists under 16 must wear a helmet on the road.
A reflective vest must be worn at night and in poor visibility.

From dusk to full daylight, and in reduced visibility, a bike must show one white light at the front and one red light at the rear; reflectors on pedals/wheels and a red rear reflector are required equipment.
Groups of two or more cyclists must ride one behind the other (single file).
Use a cycle path or lane where one exists; otherwise keep as far right as possible.
Children: from 14 a person may ride a bicycle on the road; from 9 with a school cycling certificate; other children from 9 only accompanied by someone 16 or older.

events.name: Zadar GranFondo Falkensteiner Borik (7th edition)
events.place: Start/finish Falkensteiner Resort Borik, Zadar; route through northern Zadar County, past Nin and over the Vir bridge and back.
events.distances: 56 km and 112 km (granfondoguide) or 56 km and 128 km (Falkensteiner); riders choose shortly before the start. Entry limit 500.
events.description: International amateur road race on the roads around the villa; a natural hook for autumn cycling packages in future years (the route passes within a few km of Sabunike).

officialRoutesNearby.description: Official Zadar County Tourist Board "Zadar Bike Magic" routes (2024 Zadar & Nin Riviera map) within easy reach of the villa; GPS tracks and an offline app are at zadarbikemagic.com. The board states the routes are not formal bikeways and it does not guarantee their condition.

routes.via: St Kate's and St Vid's churches
Žerava - Poljica - Vrsi - Jasenovo Bay - Nin

marketingAngles.text: Villa as a base for every bike type: 1 family loop at the door, 2 island rides, 1 gravel coves day, 3 big road days and 1 Velebit epic, all starting at the driveway with no car needed except for the optional Obrovac start.
Rent a Bike Nin advertises free delivery to apartment addresses, so guests can arrive by plane and still ride on day one.
Autumn GranFondo weekend (mid-October) and the March-May / September-November shoulder seasons fill the gap when Booking.com demand for beach stays is low.

openQuestions: Does the villa offer secure bike storage (lockable room/garage), a wash spot, a track pump and basic tools? Cyclist-friendly claims depend on it.
Is the owner willing to arrange bike rental delivery (e.g. with Rent a Bike Nin) or e-bike rental for guests? Need current prices and whether they rent e-bikes or road bikes.
Should the Mali Alan route be promoted at all given the gravel surface and landmine caveat, or shown only as the car-assisted Obrovac variant?
Which "Ričina" beach does the owner mean: Uvala Ričina near Vrsi (used in the gravel route) or the Ričina beach on north-east Vir?
Official rule on cycling over the Vir bridge (Komoot labels the footway as push-only); confirm with Općina Vir or the police before advising guests.
Is the Zaton Holiday Resort bike rental still open to non-guests, and at what price?
Does Enduro Bike Service Zadar still exist (its website did not resolve)?
Gravel route surfaces (Vrsi-Ljubač) come from a router, not a ridden GPX; the owner or a local rider should ride or check them once before publishing.
Interest in packaging the Zadar GranFondo (October) for 2027: confirm next date with the organiser.
Web search budget ran out before Croatian traffic counts, Paklenica NP cycling rules and official bura closure rules for cyclists could be checked.
